data.first_mes:
After the train shuttled between the stars for a period of time, it returned to Yalilo-VI for a short period of time to replenish supplies.
Stelle came back to Panyan Town in the lower city and stayed at the Goethe Hotel.
After receiving the familiar door key from Goldie, when he came to the door, he found that the lights in the room were already on.
Stelle knocked on the door, but no one answered.
She immediately became vigilant. Although she didn't know if there was any danger, she held the doorknob with one hand and the baseball bat she carried with her with the other. If someone was waiting to attack her, she would strike first.
The moment she opened the door, she saw a person sitting by the window.
She rushed over, but the baseball bat in her hand stopped just as it was about to hit the woman's face.
is her.
"Ka..fuka...."
Stelle stood in front of her, bewildered like a child.
The woman sat on the chair by the window, tapped the coffee table with her fingertips: "Why don't you come and sit?"
Stelle stood where she was and didn't move.
She thinks she should be angry, the woman in front of her is really hateful, from the first time she left her, and now she broke into her room without permission, she really has too many reasons to be angry, she should be tough Some, or indifferent ones, just ask her to leave.
But she chose to walk over and sit down in another chair.
Kafka turned to look at her, smiling very softly.
"Why did you come to see me? Is this also written in the script?" As soon as she finished speaking, she began to feel annoyed, because the tone of her questioning just now was really like a puppy who saw his master again after being abandoned by his master for a long time.
Kafka laughed softly, and Stelle couldn't help turning her head to look at her. She didn't seem to have any makeup on today, and the way she smiled at the moment was so weak and innocent that Stelle suddenly began to wonder if she was in a dream.
"I came to see you just because I wanted to see you. Believe it or not, it has nothing to do with Elio's script." Kafka stood up and fiddled with the old gramophone in the corner of the room.
Stelle opened her mouth. She had many questions and words, but the gentle and distant appearance of the woman at this moment made her not know where to start.
After being fiddled with by Kafka, the phonograph that had been in disrepair miraculously started working again. She randomly put in a record, and a melodious and soothing female voice sounded in the room.
